title: Tiberius Prosecutions for Magic Under Treason Laws
description: During the reign of Tiberius (14-37 CE), multiple prosecutions were conducted in which magic charges were combined with treason (maiestas) accusations, creating a powerful legal weapon against political enemies. The crimen maiestatis could subsume veneficium charges, meaning that alleged magical consultation of astrologers to determine the emperor's lifespan became treasonable. Tacitus records several such cases in the Annals, noting how the combination of charges made acquittal nearly impossible. This fusion of magic with treason prefigures the later medieval pattern of combining witchcraft with heresy and political conspiracy.
historiographical_note: Ramsay MacMullen and Richard Gordon have analyzed Tiberian prosecutions as establishing the dangerous precedent of combining magic with political conspiracy charges, a pattern with long-lasting consequences for later heresy and witchcraft accusations.
source_method: Published scholarship; Tacitus Annals 2.27-32, 4.52; secondary scholarship
